name: centrifuge-rotor-band
title: Centrifuge Rotor Band
description: An ambient 'working' indicator rendered as a benchtop microcentrifuge spin-up/hold/brake cycle combined with density-gradient ultracentrifugation banding: a rotor accelerates to speed, holds, then brakes back to rest, while four pre-loaded density bands in a sample tube drift outward under centrifugal force during each hold phase, then reload for the next run.
useWhen: Pick centrifuge-rotor-band for an ambient, indeterminate 'working' state with real physical process structure — spin-up, hold, and brake are visibly distinct phases, and the four bands sweeping outward during hold give a viewer something concrete to track without exposing a percentage. Pick loader-pendulum-sync instead for a wait long enough the user will look away and come back, where a drift-out-of-sync-and-return arc over ~10s is the legible tell; pick loader-thread-spool instead once a byte total is known and the indicator should convert into a real gauge; pick progress-hatch instead for an ordinary determinate fill with no phased process to show.
instruction: Build <CentrifugeRotorBand label? height? className?> as a card-scale <canvas> panel, an ambient 'working' indicator rendered as a benchtop microcentrifuge spin-up/hold/brake cycle combined with density-gradient ultracentrifugation banding (Svedberg sedimentation). SOURCE: a rotor accelerates to operating speed, holds, then brakes back to rest, while a sample tube's pre-loaded density bands drift outward under the applied centrifugal force during the hold phase — real bench mechanics, not an invented category. REAL NUMBERS: spin-up ramps 0 -> 14,000rpm linearly over 4.5s (RAMP_S, ~3,100rpm/s), hold sustains 14,000rpm for 8s (HOLD_S), brake decelerates 14,000 -> 0rpm linearly over 6s (BRAKE_S, slower than the accel ramp — a regenerative brake, not a hard stop). Full cycle is 18.5s (CYCLE_S), unbounded repeat via `t % CYCLE_S`. DECOUPLING: the literal 14,000rpm figure is documented in code comments and here only — rendering it 1:1 would alias against a ~60Hz paint rate into a strobe (the exact round-9 legibility failure this registry has already shipped once via meter-matrix-scan's 240Hz row-scan). The rendered spin instead uses a decoupled rpm-fraction (0..1, current rpm / 14,000) multiplied by a hard visual cap of 3 rev/s (VISUAL_REV_CAP); rotor angle is integrated every frame as `angle += 2*PI*visualRevPerSec*dtSeconds` using real elapsed time, not derived from the cycle clock directly. RENDER MODE CROSSFADE: spokes and the blurred ring crossfade continuously over rpm-fraction 0.45-0.55 (BLUR_MID +- BLUR_HALF_WIDTH) — never a hard cut, so the transition shows departure and arrival rather than a blink. Spokes (SPOKE_COUNT=3, 120° apart, from 15% to 95% of rotor radius, foreground stroke 1.5px, plus a 3px filled hub) fade out at `spokeWeight = 1 - blurWeight`; the blurred ring fades in at `blurWeight`, and its own alpha/width/radius keep varying continuously with rpm-fraction across the whole 0.5-1.0 range — outer-band alpha `(0.18 + 0.22*rpmFraction) * blurWeight`, band width `rotorRadius * (0.22 + 0.14*rpmFraction)`, band radius fraction `0.68 + 0.14*rpmFraction`, plus a thinner higher-alpha `(0.3 + 0.3*rpmFraction) * blurWeight` outer-edge stroke — so a mid-ramp frame (rpm-fraction ~0.56) and a full-hold frame (rpm-fraction 1.0) render as visibly different ring states, not the same shape twice; the paint never aliases into a strobe at the visual cap. GEOMETRY: rotor radius = min(containerWidth, containerHeight) * 0.32 (ROTOR_RADIUS_FRACTION), so the whole rig holds its shape at card scale regardless of aspect ratio; tube length, tube width and band radius are all fractions of rotor radius / tube length rather than fixed px (see BANDS below), so nothing goes imperceptible at a taller or shorter card. WOBBLE: a damped rotor-imbalance wobble (±0.4px ceiling, WOBBLE_MAX_PX) offsets the rotor's own center via `wobbleAmp * sin(t*23.1)` / `cos(t*17.3)` on independent axes, gated by `max(0, (rpmFraction-0.4)/0.6)` clamped to 1 — present only above 40% of the current rpm-fraction (WOBBLE_ONSET_FRACTION), silent below it, and forced to zero for the reduced-motion freeze frame so that frame is genuinely static. TUBE: a fixed-orientation sample tube slot (0°, straight up from the rotor's center, NOT rotating with the rotor's own spin phase — a deliberate legibility choice so the bands stay trackable rather than blurring into the rotor's motion) is drawn as a rounded capsule, length = rotor radius * 0.9 (TUBE_LENGTH_FRACTION), width = rotor radius * 0.075 (TUBE_WIDTH_FRACTION), filled with `--background` and stroked with `--ns-muted`. BANDS: four density bands at starting radii 22% / 38% / 55% / 71% of the tube's length (BAND_START_FRACTIONS), each a filled `--foreground` dot of radius = rotor radius * 0.05 (BAND_RADIUS_FRACTION — deliberately a touch wider than half the tube's own width, so a band visibly protrudes past the tube edge rather than disappearing inside it). Offset applied to every band's start radius is one continuous function of cycle time, never a discrete step within a phase: during ramp it eases linearly from 0 to `-compression` (BAND_COMPRESSION_FRACTION=0.05 of tube length — a very slight inward drift from inertial lag as speed climbs); during hold it sweeps linearly from `-compression` to `+migration` (BAND_MIGRATION_FRACTION=0.14 of tube length — the steady continuous outward drift across the 8s hold, exaggerated from the real sub-pixel Svedberg rate for legibility, and the ONE thing a viewer should follow); during brake it holds at the full `+migration` value (bands do not reset until the cycle itself rolls over — a real prep is reloaded between runs, so that snap back to 0 at the top of the next cycle is mechanically honest, not a cheat; it is the only sanctioned discontinuity in the whole offset curve). Migration/compression are expressed as fractions of the tube's own length (itself derived from the container's smaller dimension) rather than fixed px, specifically so the drift stays perceptible whether the card is short or tall. RESTING LOOP: t0 — rotor at rest (rpm-fraction 0, three static spokes visible, hub only), four bands at their unmigrated start radii, tube fully visible; 2.5s — rotor mid-ramp (rpm-fraction ~0.56, already past the blur crossfade midpoint so the blurred ring dominates over the fading spokes), bands compressed slightly toward center; 5s — 0.5s into the hold, rpm-fraction pinned at 1.0 so the ring sits at its full-speed alpha/width/radius — visibly more solid and wider than the 2.5s ramp-state ring, which is the primary tell that time has passed at that checkpoint — while the bands have just begun their outward sweep off the ramp's compressed floor. Unbounded, zero input, alive at rest. TOKENS: fg/muted/bg are read once via `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement)` against `--foreground` / `--ns-muted` / `--background` before the first paint (no paint before the first read), re-derived on a documentElement class MutationObserver so a theme flip repaints live. `--ns-muted` is the housing ring's own stroke and the tube's outline (a 2-stop foreground/ns-muted luminance ramp, never a fill on the climactic band motion); `--foreground` is the spokes/blurred-ring/hub/bands; `--background` is the tube's own fill, so bands must read as visibly darker dots against a lighter tube slot in light theme specifically — verify that contrast at every migration step, since light theme is where value-only readability breaks first. No `--border` usage (nothing here is a separator) and `--ns-accent` never appears — there is no interactive affordance in this build; a future hover state may only brighten band luminance, never mix accent into it. REDUCED MOTION: freezes at cycle t=8.7s (FREEZE_T) — the hold-phase midpoint — rendering the rotor as a static translucent ring at full speed (no motion-blur trail, no strobing, no wobble, since the freeze is a single deterministic draw call with wobble amplitude forced to zero) with bands at mid-migration (52.5% of the way from the ramp-end compressed position to the hold-end fully-migrated position, `(8.7-4.5)/8 = 0.525` of the hold's own sweep). This is the single most structured frame: both the spin state and the band drift are legible without motion. Checked via `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` at mount, no live-change listener needed since the component has no other motion state to reconcile. LIFECYCLE: canvas sized via `getBoundingClientRect` with `devicePixelRatio` (capped at 2) applied through `ctx.setTransform`, resize handled by a debounced ResizeObserver (150ms), the rAF loop paused by an IntersectionObserver when off-screen and by `document.hidden` via a visibilitychange listener (both resume with a fresh last-timestamp, no giant delta-time jump), and every rAF/observer/listener is torn down on unmount. A11Y: the canvas itself is `aria-hidden` (decorative raster); it is wrapped in a `role=img` element carrying an `aria-label` summarizing the reading in prose ('a centrifuge rotor spinning up, holding, and braking, while four sample density bands drift outward each hold cycle') since a continuously-cycling phased process has no single scalar `aria-valuenow` to expose the way an ordinary progress bar would. Below the label row, a static Geist Mono caption row reads the two REAL NUMBERS that never change — '14,000 RPM' / '18.5s CYCLE' — so those constants are legible from a single still frame independent of motion. No canvas colour literal, no dependency: 2D canvas, DOM+canvas+CSS only. Props: label (accessible name and visible caption, default 'Rotor speed'), height (canvas panel height px, default 220), className.
